clue.text: Site of many casinos: card cut in one

indicators.note: something cut has lost a piece, here its final letter
in places the shortened card inside the word for one

parts.note: mono- is the prefix meaning one, used as a word for single
the card is an ACE, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A gambler in a casino town has a card game interrupted by a cut of the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like cutting the deck before a deal, but it trims a letter from the card.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean principality is famous for Monte Carlo and its gambling houses.

clue.text: Obvious industrial action?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: conspicuous, catching the eye
second meaning: walking out of work in protest

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests a blatant strike; the question mark flags that the word for a walkout also means noticeable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means conspicuous or remarkable, and the participle names workers downing tools in a dispute.

clue.text: A piece of cake in hand to be given to dependant

parts.note: a straight is a poker hand of five consecutive cards
a present given to someone is for them
a ward is a child dependent on a guardian

explanation.surface: A slice of cake handed over to someone who relies on you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like food, but it is the idiom for something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a piece of cake is simple and uncomplicated to do.

clue.text: Groovy touring America, very close to city in Texas

indicators.note: something touring goes round, so these letters wrap around the country

parts.note: hot can mean fashionable, much like groovy
the usual abbreviation for the United States
on can mean right beside, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A hip band touring the States plays a city in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' and 'very close' both lean on informal senses: hot as fashionable, on as right beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston is the largest city in the American state of Texas.

clue.text: Lift isn't cheaper to repair, initially

indicators.note: repairing something means taking it apart and putting it together differently

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Fixing a broken elevator at the start would not save any money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letters signal, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Initially and in the first place are both phrases meaning at the start or originally.

clue.text: Constitutional crisis's ultimate troublemaker online

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of crisis
a troll posts provocative messages on the internet

explanation.surface: A constitutional crisis is stirred up by an internet agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' reads as political, but a constitutional is also an old-fashioned word for a health-giving walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a leisurely walk taken for health, the same as a gentle amble.

clue.text: Hurt, a cook cut

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its end, here the final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a cook is a CHEF, with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: A chef in the kitchen nicks a finger and is hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt as a verb can mean to be sore or painful, the same sense as the word for a dull pain.

clue.text: Left Felixstowe, for example?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone departing Felixstowe; Felixstowe is a major container port in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the left side of a vessel by this name, and it also means a harbour town.

clue.text: Initially teeth wonky: order a brace

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of three words

explanation.surface: A dentist decides crooked teeth call for fitting a brace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' suggests orthodontics, but a brace is also a pair, as in a brace of pheasants.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, the number of things in a couple.

clue.text: Testament embraced by particular see

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: nice can mean fussy or exacting, as in a nice distinction
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Scripture is cherished by a particular bishop's diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a bishop's diocese in this surface but is the verb to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to observe or spot it, just as to see it.

clue.text: Wreck occupying a harbour

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or wreck
occupying a place means being in it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipwreck sits in the middle of a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a small harbour for yachts and pleasure boats.

clue.text: A shipping vessel?

parts.note: surface reading: a boat used to carry cargo
setter's reading: a container for drink that is both a sailing ship and a tall glass

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is both a two-masted sailing ship and a large glass for sherry or beer, so it is literally a vessel twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship and also a tall drinking glass.

clue.text: Take in lovely chap, mischievous character

parts.note: to rob is to take unlawfully
taken as written
a good fellow is a fine, likeable man

explanation.surface: A charming man is swindled by a prankster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like a phrasal verb for deceive, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Goodfellow is the English folklore sprite also known as Puck, famous for pranks.

clue.text: Recite outstanding poem

indicators.note: reciting is saying out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a debt outstanding is still owed

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to perform an excellent poem from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' wants to mean excellent; here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject, often in praise.

clue.text: Easy raids by Britain during the war

indicators.note: raiders break into a place, so one word enters the other

parts.note: taken as written, split to hold the other piece
light work is easy

explanation.surface: Wartime Britain suffered only easy air raids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raids' reads as bombing, but here it means breaks into. Blighty was soldiers' slang for Britain or home in the World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighty is the affectionate slang name British troops abroad used for home, especially in the First World War.

clue.text: Sign put up in Tokyo, electrified

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means read from the bottom upwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A neon sign is hung high in Tokyo with the power switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Haggard novel in classic, ruined

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: trad, short for traditional, means classic
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.surface: A Victorian adventure story in a classic edition has been damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' looks like the adjective for gaunt, but it is the novelist Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is informal for wrecked or destroyed, the same as ruined.

clue.text: Scary criminal practice somewhere in Sicily

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder
use is custom or practice

explanation.surface: Frightening Mafia activity goes on in a part of Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Syracuse is an ancient port city on the east coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Decent angle capturing mood

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line
an air is an atmosphere or mood

explanation.surface: A fair-minded fisherman catches the mood of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angle' suggests geometry or a viewpoint; here it is the verb to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairish means reasonably good, much like decent in the sense of adequate.

clue.text: Wrong waterproof on, yet right legally

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a mac in the wrong conditions is still technically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A power of attorney is a legal authority granted to act for someone else, a right conferred by law.

clue.text: Join up squiggly lines on bottom of portrait

indicators.note: squiggly lines are wavy and twisted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

parts.note: the final letter of portrait

explanation.surface: An artist joins up wavy lines at the base of a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join up' looks like the artist's action; it is the definition, meaning sign up for service.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up for military service, which is to join up.

clue.text: Contents of vent and exhaust complete

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, without the outer ones

parts.note: the inner letters of vent
to tire is to exhaust

explanation.surface: Air from the vent and the exhaust pipe has been fully expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exhaust' looks like the car part, but here it is the verb to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: Found in river, cold shorn sheep

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside the other

parts.note: a flower is crossword shorthand for a river, something that flows

indicators.note: shorn means clipped all round, so the outside letters are lost

parts.note: the word cold without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sheep with a fresh fleece clipping is discovered in a chilly river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheep' looks like an animal, but it is the definition in its figurative sense: someone who goes along with the crowd. A flower is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep, figuratively, is a person who meekly follows others, just as a follower does.

clue.text: Some buffalo, great big beast

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a buffalo herd is a great hulking animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a huge, brutish monster of folklore.

clue.text: Embroidered lace to pin down

indicators.note: embroidered means worked into a new pattern, or embellished, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A seamstress pins decorated lace in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to find its exact position, to pin it down.

clue.text: Rare set, almost misplaced, in schoolboy's possession?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
misplaced letters are put in the wrong positions, so they are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
set with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A collector's rare set has been lost, though a schoolboy may have it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: a rubber is a typical thing in a pupil's pencil case, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser, or rubber, is a standard item of school stationery that a pupil would carry.

clue.text: Endless suffering: that's right, though appears wrong

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: suffering is SICK, minus its end

explanation.surface: Someone in pain insists they're correct even though it looks otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors insert the Latin 'sic' to show a quoted error is reproduced exactly as in the original.

clue.text: Organise type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to arrange in order
second meaning: a kind or category

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to arrange print; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for arranging things and a noun for a kind or variety.
